crm.module-state.summaryTemplate: Authoritative {module} state from the installed CRM runtime with {recordCount} returned records.

invariants: Capabilities express compatible operations, never permission grants.
A control target is a live visible anchor; business field meaning comes from application field definitions and component state.
Editable field controls close the field-to-control-to-operation-to-commit-to-verification loop when a commit control is present.
Field inventory distinguishes schema presence, layout reachability, and current live binding; the existence of a record attribute never implies that a UI route exists.
Choice bindings distinguish the human semantic label from the exact action argument and require unchanged post-action state to be treated as a failed transition.
Opaque localization keys are never semantic labels; resolve them through application translation resources or a declared authoritative field-name fallback.
Relationship comboboxes, query inputs, live option overlays, and selected values preserve the parent field identity and remain in the editable-choice priority class.
Each live relationship option has one canonical executable Binding; non-actionable descendants are semantic context and never interaction targets.

Relationship query text, candidate entities, unresolved transitions, and selected entities are distinct states; query text never emits the business field current-value fact, and a pending query is transaction-scoped across local visibility changes. It suppresses commit until a post-query selected-identity transition, matching canonical candidate activation plus selected state, declared cancellation, or transaction-surface exit; a pre-query selected value alone is not completion evidence.
Interaction Bindings expose at least one declared executable operation; contextual descendants without operations remain outside the actionable Binding collection.
Unknown, blank, duplicate, or stale bindings fail closed instead of being guessed from benchmark task text.
